function_description: Retrieves the autoscaling margin of the z-axis.
code_example:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from mpl_toolkits.mplot3d import Axes3D

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(111, projection='3d')
print(ax.get_zmargin())

function_description: Removes minor ticks from the axis.
code_example:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.minorticks_off()

function_description: Aligns the titles of subplots in the same row when title alignment is automatic.
code_example:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 2)
axs[0].set_title('Title 0')
axs[1].set_title('Title 1')
fig.align_titles()
parameters: axs: list of Axes, optional. List of Axes to align the titles. Default is to align all Axes on the figure.
note: This assumes that all Axes in axs are from the same GridSpec, so that their SubplotSpec positions correspond to figure positions.

function_description: Retrieves the autoscaling margin of the y-axis.
code_example:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
margin = ax.get_ymargin()
print(margin)

function_description: Enables minor ticks on the Axis based on the current scale.
code_example:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.minorticks_on()
note: Displaying minor ticks may reduce performance; use minorticks_off() to disable them if needed.

function_description: Returns the autoscaling margin for the x-axis.
code_example:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
print(ax.get_xmargin())

function_description: Fills the area between two 3D curves defined by their coordinates.
code_example:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from mpl_toolkits.mplot3d import Axes3D

fig = plt.figure()
ax = Axes3D(fig)
x1 = [0, 1, 2]
y1 = [0, 1, 0]
z1 = [0, 0, 0]
x2 = [0, 1, 2]
y2 = [0, 0, 0]
z2 = [0, 0, 0]
ax.fill_between(x1, y1, z1, x2, y2, z2)
